pi.name: Cunming Duan
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Cunming Duan is a Professor in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the University of Michigan. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Tokyo and completed postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Washington and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. His lab studies the regulation, function, and evolution of nutrient-sensitive insulin and insulin-like growth factor (IIS) signaling and how it controls cellular plasticity under stresses such as hypoxia, nutrient deficiency, and acidosis, with recent work extending to calcium metabolism, bone mineralization, renal mineral balance, and hypoxia biology.

description: The Duan lab investigates the molecular mechanisms governing cell cycle plasticity during tissue formation, growth, and regeneration. Using a zebrafish model in which differentiated epithelial cells can be induced to re-enter the cell cycle in response to stress, the lab asks how cells decide between quiescence and proliferation when faced with changing nutrient availability, oxygen levels, and pH. The group's approaches include CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, in vivo imaging, chemical biology, and RNA-seq. Many of the regulators the lab has discovered converge on the insulin/insulin-like growth factor (IIS)-PI3 kinase-Akt-TOR signaling pathway. The lab also studies hypoxia and HIF biology, stanniocalcins, and calcium homeostasis.

areas.title: Tissue formation, growth, and regeneration
areas.summary: The lab examines how the insulin/IGF (IIS)-PI3K-Akt-TOR signaling pathway regulates cell cycle plasticity when cells encounter varying nutrient, oxygen, and pH conditions during tissue maintenance and healing, using a zebrafish epithelial cell reactivation model.

areas.title: Hypoxia and HIF biology
areas.summary: The lab studies how hypoxia signaling, including stanniocalcins, shapes IGF-stimulated growth versus organismal survival under hypoxic stress.
